newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Maastricht must be seen "as a whole".
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Maastricht must be seen "as a whole".

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday the Maastricht Treaty, which contains guidelines for membership in the single European currency, should be looked at "as a whole."
"Despite all the current discussions about budget deficits and inflation rates, we should see the Maastricht Treaty as a whole," Waigel said in the text of a speech to a local group.

"In the age of globalisation of economies and financial markets, and the worldwide creation of economic blocs, Europe needs a single economic area with a common currency in order to preserve its economic competitiveness and standard of living," Waigel said.
He added that those who did not agree with the direction in which European politics were currently moving were putting the political decline of European states on the line.
"One of the major arguments against Maastricht are always the arguments that it is coming too early and coming too fast. All I can say to that is hopefully it is not too late," Waigel said.
